findings.title: Ownership check removed from getOwnedAccount: any user can act on any account
findings.description: The branch that compared account.ownerId with userId and threw 403 FORBIDDEN was deleted. getOwnedAccount now returns any existing account to any authenticated caller, so every route that relies on it for authorization (reading an account, choosing the source account of a transfer) is open to broken object-level authorization (IDOR).
findings.evidence:
if (account.ownerId !== userId) {
throw new AppError(403, 'FORBIDDEN', 'You do not own this account');
findings.impact: Any signed-in user can read another user's balance and transfer money out of another user's account.
findings.recommendation: Restore the ownerId comparison and the 403 FORBIDDEN error, and keep the cross-account tests.

findings.title: getOwnedAccount no longer matches its contract; userId is now unused
findings.description: The doc comment says the account is returned only if it belongs to userId, and the name promises ownership, but the ownership branch was removed. The userId parameter is now dead, which hides the regression from callers.
findings.impact: Every caller silently loses an authorization guarantee it relies on.
findings.recommendation: Restore the check; if ownership must be optional, add a separate, explicitly named function.

findings.title: Cross-account authorization tests will fail and must not be weakened
findings.description: test/api.test.ts expects 403 when Bob reads or transfers from Alice's account. With the check removed these tests fail. The PR changes no tests, so either CI is red or the tests get deleted to make it pass.

findings.impact: If the tests are edited to pass, the bypass ships with no regression guard.
